newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MYTILINEOS SAYS 96 SALES, PROFITS SHARPLY UP. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GREEK MYTILINEOS SAYS 96 SALES, PROFITS SHARPLY UP. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]

text.p: Greek metals trading firm Mytilineos said in a statement that its consolidated pretax profits rose sharply 67.1 percent to 1.21 billion drachmas in 1996 from 724 million in 1995.
Consolidated sales surged 50.3 percent to 26 billion drachmas (corrects) from 17.3 billion in 1995 on the back of its fast growing international business, it said.
"In 1996, Mytilineos boosted its international activities and group sales to third countries reached 8.6 billion drachmas against 1.8 billion in 1995," it said.
The management of the firm predicted that the high growth rates would be sustained in 1997 and the firm remained committed to expanding its international business.
New cooperation agreements in minerals and base metals will be announced at the general shareholders meeting, it added.
Mytilineos said the prevailing conditions in international markets were very favourable with the group benefiting from price increases in all metals and iron and the strong rise of the dollar.
"..more than 80 percent of company sales are in dollars or in other currencies but indexed to the dollar," it added.
The new bonus shares of the firm will start trading on the Athens bourse today.
